blueprints.title: Alert → incident triage
blueprints.description: Watch Alertmanager; when an alert fires, investigate metrics and logs, build a timeline, summarise, and propose (never run) a rollback when a recent deploy is the likely cause.
blueprints.prompt_template: Follow the incident-response skill (references/oncall-runbook.md). 1) alertmanager_alerts kind=alerts active=true with filter severity=~"{severity}"; if nothing fired or changed since the last run, respond with [SILENT]. 2) For each new alert group: query the alert's expression and neighbours with prometheus_query (range over the last hour), pull matching error lines with loki_query or elastic_search, and check deploy action=history plus grafana_query annotations for changes in the last 2 hours. 3) Write the timeline (UTC, oldest first), the impact, the most likely cause with evidence, and open questions. 4) If a deploy correlates, propose `deploy action=rollback plan_id=<id>` with the reason — do not run it; the on-call human approves. 5) Offer to open or update a ticket (jira / servicenow / pagerduty) with this summary.

slots.label: How often?
slots.help: minutes between checks

slots.label: Which alerts?
slots.help: Alertmanager severity label values (regex)

blueprints.title: Weekly vulnerability triage
blueprints.description: Parse the latest scanner reports, de-duplicate, rank by exploitability and draft remediation tickets for the top findings.
blueprints.prompt_template: Follow the vuln-triage skill (references/vuln-triage-runbook.md). Run scan_report over the reports in {reports} (with the KEV list when [integrations.secops] kev_file is set), output the ranked list to reports/ranked-<date>.csv, and look up the P1/P2 package findings with osv_query for fixed versions. Group findings that one change fixes (same package / base image). Draft one ticket per group with priority, evidence, fix and owner hint, and list them; create them with jira or servicenow only after the user approves the list. Never run scanners against hosts here.
